items.item: Q1. What was compared in run 3, and which arm did better (answered from the page alone)
items.evidence: From the page: one model (the 4B) in both arms, on 8 cells (the 8 stock-note tasks under the injected empty lookup). One arm replaces the `null` of an empty `lookup_order` result with a message that says to call `lookup_order` again. The other arm is run 2's set-up, where the model gets `null`. The arm with the message did better: 15 of 16 against 2 of 16. I got this from lines 113-130 without help. RESULT-run-3.md says the same. I also ran `arci report` on a scratch copy of the committed run-3 store: BLOCK, stored decision: match, baseline 15, candidate 2, minus 13 / zero 3 / plus 0, BLOCK wealth 4.27909e+01, PASS wealth 1.29680e-02.
items.fix: None needed for the content. See the items below for where a faster reader could still go wrong.

items.item: Q2. What BLOCK means in run 3, and whether it is the same as in run 1
items.evidence: The page says it plainly at lines 115-117: `BLOCK` in run 3 means that the set-up without the message passes less often, by more than the margin, and it is not a second failure of the 4B against the 12B. In run 1 `BLOCK` meant the 4B candidate was worse than the 12B baseline. RESULT-run-3.md ('Read this first: the roles are swapped') agrees.

'with and without a message at the point of failure, and its arm roles are swapped' needed two reads: what message, and swapped relative to what, are not said.
items.fix: Replace lines 10-13 with: "**Run 3 is a different comparison.** It does not compare the two models. Both arms use the 4B model. The arm with the message passed more often. The tool prints this result as `BLOCK`, because the arm without the message is labelled the candidate. items.item: Q9b. The linked pre-registration states a run 2 figure that the store does not support
